articles.title: “Someone else will clean it”: The mindset Bittu Tabahi challenged by cleaning a river alone and the psychology of doing what everyone else ignores
articles.description: Surendra Singh Choudhary, affectionately called Bittu Tabahi, took it upon himself to personally cleanse the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh. By investing his own resources and labor, he tackled the pressing issue of pollution. Bittu's commitment serves as a powerful reminder of how collective responsibility can sometimes lead to inaction, urging us to embrace personal accountability and inspire proactive efforts to restore our environment.

articles.title: Amit Shah speaks to Delhi CM, top officials after building collapse
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke with Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and other senior officials after a five-storey building near Delhi University's south campus collapsed, leaving one dead and several trapped in the rubble. In a message posted on X, Shah said he was deeply distressed by the building collapse at Satya Niketan in Delhi. "Spoke with the chief minister, commissioner of police, Delhi, and the director general, NDRF, and assessed the situation on the ground," he said. Shah said the local administration and the NDRF are conducting intensive rescue operations in close coordination. "The injured are being provided with all necessary medical assistance. Praying for the speedy recovery of all those injured," he said. The 50-year-old building housing a boys' hostel collapsed in a congested bylane in Satya Niketan near DU's south campus on Sunday afternoon, officials said. Six people have been pulled out of the debris so far, of whom one was brought dead to the hospital

articles.title: VHP Bans 'Muslims’ From Garba Celebrations or Events | Aadhaar, Tilak Checks in Maharashtra | News
articles.description: A fresh controversy has erupted in Maharashtra ahead of Navratri after the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) announced that Muslims should not be allowed to participate in Garba and Dandiya events across the state.The VHP has also issued guidelines for event organisers, including checking attendees’ Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on their foreheads to verify what it describes as the Hindu identity of participants. The guidelines come ahead of Navratri, which begins on October 11 this year.VHP spokesperson and joint secretary Shriraj Nair defended the move, saying Navratri is a religious festival centred on worship of the Goddess and that the organisation wants to protect the cultural character of Hindu festivals. The VHP has described the measures as precautionary, while critics have raised questions over religious discrimination, identity checks and access to public cultural events.The controversy is also significant because it comes shortly after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke about universal oneness and the dignity of all people during his New York address. The VHP has declined to comment on Bhagwat’s remarks.Is this about preserving the religious character of Navratri — or does it cross the line into religious exclusion?Watch this LIVE coverage for the latest political reactions, the VHP’s guidelines and the growing Maharashtra Garba-Dandiya row. -news CNN-News18 is your trusted source for breaking news, updates, and in-depth analysis from around the world.
